applies_why: The judge counts verses (Matthew 1:18, 25; Luke 1:34) against the challenger's link as unanswered witnesses without quoting the sentence of the earlier round that pressed them against that link or naming that round.
quote: [L1] Matthew 1:18 ... and Matthew 1:25 ... contradict C3's claim of espousal union; [L2] πρὶν ἢ συνελθεῖν ... [L3] Luke 1:34.
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count.
room: 'pressed it against that link': whether listing verses as links breaking a claim without quoting any earlier-round pressing sentence counts as pressing; I weighed the judge's own citation as sufficient versus the rule's explicit requirement of a quoted sentence and named round.
why: No earlier round is named and no earlier-round sentence is quoted, so the verses cannot count as pressed witnesses, yet the judge uses them to declare the link broken.
